report_name: Bitter APT Targets South Asia with New C++/Rust PapRAT Backdoor

threat_actors.name: Bitter
threat_actors.description: A cyber espionage group conducting a new campaign targeting organizations in South Asia with a previously undocumented remote access trojan (RAT) named PapRAT. The group uses complex infection chains involving LNK files, VHDX images, and WebDAV servers.
threat_actors.goals: The primary goal of the Bitter group is espionage, including long-term intelligence gathering and data exfiltration of sensitive government or defense information.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Attachment
attack_patterns.description: The initial delivery of the malware likely involves phishing emails containing malicious LNK, VHDX, or URL files as attachments.

attack_patterns.name: User Execution: Malicious File
attack_patterns.description: The campaign relies on the victim executing malicious LNK and URL files to initiate the infection chain.

attack_patterns.name: Mark-of-the-Web Bypass
attack_patterns.description: The use of VHDX disk images to deliver malicious LNK files can bypass Mark-of-the-Web security warnings.

attack_patterns.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Rundll32
attack_patterns.description: Malicious LNK files were observed calling rundll32.exe to execute malicious code.

attack_patterns.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
attack_patterns.description: A remote WebDAV server was used for command and control communications and to deliver a malicious LNK file payload.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
attack_patterns.description: The Rust variant of the PapRAT backdoor is capable of executing PowerShell commands for in-memory execution and potential lateral movement.

attack_patterns.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
attack_patterns.description: The infection chain establishes persistence on the compromised system by creating scheduled tasks.

attack_patterns.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
attack_patterns.description: The legitimate Windows utility ftp.exe was abused via a malicious LNK file to download scripts from a remote server.

attack_patterns.name: Screen Capture
attack_patterns.description: The PapRAT backdoor has the capability to capture screenshots of the victim's desktop.

malware.name: PapRAT
malware.description: A previously undocumented remote access trojan (RAT) deployed by the Bitter APT group. It exists in both C++ and Rust versions and is delivered through malicious LNK files, VHDX images, and WebDAV servers to provide remote control over compromised systems.

tools.name: ftp.exe
tools.description: The legitimate ftp.exe utility was abused by a malicious LNK file to download scripts from a remote server.

tools.name: Rundll32
tools.description: The legitimate Windows utility rundll32.exe is used by malicious LNK files to execute malicious code.

tools.name: Msiexec
tools.description: The legitimate Windows Installer utility msiexec.exe is used to execute the malicious MSI installer for the PapRAT backdoor.

infrastructure.name: PapRAT Script Hosting Server
infrastructure.description: A remote server, goodnfortunes.com, was used to host malicious scripts downloaded by ftp.exe during the infection chain.

infrastructure.name: PapRAT WebDAV C2 Server
infrastructure.description: A remote WebDAV server was used for command and control and to deliver a malicious LNK file as part of one of the infection chains.

indicators.name: Bitter APT PapRAT C2 Domain
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Bitter APT PapRAT C2 DNS Query
id: 2b8a1c9d-f3e4-4b1a-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS queries to a domain used by Bitter APT to host malicious scripts for the PapRAT backdoor.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/bitter-hackers-deploy-new-paprat.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-09
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.command_and_control
level: high
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|contains:
      - 'goodnfortunes.com'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects network connections to the domain goodnfortunes.com, which is known to be used by the Bitter APT to host malicious scripts for the PapRAT backdoor.

indicators.name: Suspicious FTP Script Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious FTP Script Execution
id: 5d9e8f7a-6b4c-4d3e-8a1b-2c3d4e5f6a7b
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of ftp.exe with the '-s' parameter, which indicates it is running a script. This technique was used by the Bitter APT to download payloads.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/bitter-hackers-deploy-new-paprat.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-09
tags:
  - attack.t1105
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\ftp.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: ' -s:'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of ftp.exe with the '-s' parameter, a technique used by Bitter APT to download malicious scripts.

indicators.name: Suspicious WebDAV PROPFIND Method
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious WebDAV PROPFIND Method
id: 9a8b7c6d-5e4f-4d3c-8b2a-1c9d8e7f6a5b
status: experimental
description: Detects WebDAV PROPFIND requests, which can be used for C2 communications or payload delivery, as seen in the Bitter APT campaign.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/bitter-hackers-deploy-new-paprat.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-09
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
level: low
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    cs-method: 'PROPFIND'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of the WebDAV PROPFIND method, which could indicate C2 activity similar to that of the Bitter APT.
